blocks.title: Mechanics
blocks.subtitle: How the peril works, how the score works — briefly, before the full case.

blocks.text: The market asks who breaks? The grid asks who can be switched off? — and the score must answer the second question on two axes, not one.
I · Wrong question
Two axes, one posture

Every entity is placed on two scored axes, not ranked by a single hazard score. Exposure measures the size of the bet: how much non-firm, curtailable load sits in the book or the asset, how concentrated it is on the same grid geography, and how badly today's wordings miss the peril.{{cite:ACAD-CRI-GRID-SRI,LMA-BI-GUIDE}} Preparedness measures the ability to carry it: whether the underwriter has the data, the products, the modelling, the expertise and the capital to actually hold the risk it has written.{{cite:PRA-SII-SCR,RATING-AMBEST-FSR}} The signal is not exposure alone — it is the gap between the two.

blocks.caption: The two axes cut the field into four quadrants. The warning light is a large negative margin.

cells.label: Whitespace
cells.note: Capable, under-deployed. Capacity is available here but not yet earning — the opportunity.

cells.label: Earning it
cells.note: Exposed and prepared. Carrying real non-firm risk with the data, products and capital to match.

cells.label: Sidelined
cells.note: Neither exposed nor ready. Watching from the bench while the market forms.

cells.label: Exposed
cells.note: Exposure accumulating faster than the data, products and capital to support it. The danger zone.

blocks.text: Margin of Safety = Preparedness − Exposure. Not who is exposed? — who is exposed beyond their ability to carry it?
II · Availability without damage
The peril that leaves no crater

A non-firm connection fails in a way the market's instruments do not register. There is no broken asset, no proximate physical cause, no repair. The grid operator, acting entirely within its rights, instructs a curtailment; the facility loses availability; the penalty or the lost revenue lands. A business-interruption policy that triggers on physical damage to insured property{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,INSTECH-NDBI-PARAMETRIC}} never sees it — the adjuster finds nothing to adjust.

Curtailment is a compound loss{{cite:ACT-COMP-LOSS,NESO-CONSTRAINT-COSTS}} — frequency times severity — and both terms move with grid constraints and queue position, not with the asset's physical condition. It is availability loss, not equipment failure. Covering it means a trigger that pays on an index of interruption rather than a loss adjuster's finding of damage, with the basis risk{{cite:ACAD-BASIS-RISK-EXPECTILES,ACAD-TEH-WOOLNOUGH-TRIGGER}} that any parametric line inherits — and that is not a cat tail dressed in different clothes.
III · Models that cannot see it
Cat, cyber and property were never built for curtailment

blocks.caption: Three frameworks the market already owns — and three reasons each fails structurally, not for lack of data.

items.name: Catastrophe model
items.role: Requires a geospatial hazard footprint and an event set. Curtailment has neither — the hazard is encoded in the connection agreement and the constraint map.
items.examples: Lloyd's RDS stress tests, vendor nat-cat modules

items.name: Cyber aggregation model
items.role: Prices a non-physical peril, but losses correlate through shared software, service providers and supply chains — not shared grid geography.
items.examples: Cloud outage parametric, service-provider dependency maps

items.name: Network correlation substrate
items.role: Non-firm power risk co-moves through constraint boundaries, shared Grid Supply Points and colocation — diversification from unrelated codebases does not apply.
items.examples: Constraint-cost data, TEC/ECR registers, GSP clustering

blocks.text: Better event sets will not fix the first mismatch: there is no physical footprint to map.{{cite:LLOYDS-RDS}} The peril is contractual — curtailment rights, end-dates, predictability class — sitting in a register the cat vendor never ingests.

Cyber taught the market to price interruption without damage, but aggregation runs through shared stack and vendor concentration{{cite:ACAD-AI-ENERGY-DCC,LLOYDS-PARAMETRIC-CYBER}} — not through two data centres on the same constrained feeder. Importing cyber's correlation substrate misstates the tail.

The correct substrate is the network itself: two campuses behind the same constraint boundary move together whether or not they share a codebase.{{cite:ACAD-CCM-NF-LOAD,ACT-HHI-EIOPA}} Pro-rata curtailment across heterogeneous value-of-lost-load destroys surplus — the aggregation variable is geography, not software.

Accumulation debates in other perils span orders of magnitude — cyber and grid-attack PML estimates differ by 10× or more between public agencies and market stress tests.{{cite:LLOYDS-RDS}} Non-firm availability has no equivalent consensus yet because there is no shared trigger: some desks treat curtailment as zero premium, others as a parametric upsell, still others as silent BI extension risk. The disagreement is architectural — not a shortage of historical loss data to fit.
Questions no existing model can settle

items: What is the PML when a constraint boundary curtails every flex-connected asset behind it simultaneously — and how does that differ from the sum of standalone BI limits?
Can pro-rata curtailment across heterogeneous value-of-lost-load be hedged with a single parametric index without unacceptable basis risk?
Does any filed energy BI extension pay lawful operator instruction with no physical damage — or does every wording still route through proximate cause?
How should an underwriter price a peril whose frequency rises with queue depth and whose severity is contractual, not Gaussian?

blocks.text: IV · Outside-in discipline

Every rating names its source class — register, filing, derived field, or sourced research — and links to the primary. Outside-in judgements fuse with register readings from the TEC and ECR by published credibility rules;{{cite:ACT-CREDIBILITY,NESO-TEC,NGED-ECR}} where measured share is still below gate, magnitudes stay directional rather than publication-grade. That honesty is the point: the shape of the field is visible before every sub-factor is fully measured. Full scoring pipeline: methodology.

Architecturally, the index is a discipline layer between live registers and placement: ingest NESO TEC and DNO ECR deltas, fuse them with sourced research under published λ rules, propagate L3 firmness to linked carriers, and recompute median cuts before any HTML ships. What is excluded is as important as what is scored — entities without a citable sub-factor trail stay out of the published universe; assessed preparedness ratings carry confidence caps; magnitudes below the L5 gate are labelled PROVISIONAL once, at the data handoff.
With the map and the mechanics set: three claims, one instrument.

blocks.title: Argument & proposal
blocks.subtitle: Substantiate the case, name the instrument, close on who can carry what the market has not yet priced.

blocks.text: V · A peril underwritten blind
A peril the market was not built to see

For a century the large industrial insurance contract has answered a single question: what happens if the thing breaks? That question built the property and business-interruption market. It is also, increasingly, the wrong one for the fastest-growing concentration of insured value in Britain. The dominant risk to a data centre or a grid-scale energy asset is no longer that it breaks. It is that it is lawfully, contractually, and repeatedly switched off.{{cite:ACAD-DC-OUTAGE,ACAD-NONFIRM-REVIEW}}

This essay makes three claims and proposes one instrument. First, that non-firm power risk is large, growing, and structurally mispriced — an incomplete market, not a thin market.{{cite:INSTECH-NDBI-PARAMETRIC,ACAD-CLARKE-INDEX-DEMAND}} Second, that the models the market reaches for cannot see it, for reasons that are architectural rather than incidental. Third, that pricing it correctly requires the two-axis construct above — exposure against preparedness — not a single hazard score. The instrument is an outside-in map of exactly that, reconciled from the registers and filings the placement chain already walks past.{{cite:NESO-TEC,DCUSA-ECR}}
VI · The number is large
The number is not small

If the answer were obvious — a single PML, a single CAGR, a hedgeable index — it would not be published here. The honest question for a GB energy or DC account in 2026 is simpler and harder: what premium should attach to lawful switch-off, and who in the tower is already carrying it without knowing? The stacking below is how large the gap is before anyone agrees on severity.

The data-centre build-out has put a demand queue measured in the tens of gigawatts in front of the system operator,{{cite:ACAD-DESANTI-FCA-QUEUE,OFGEM-DEMAND-REFORM}} and the connections clearing it are disproportionately the flexible, curtailable kind. A hyperscale facility contracts for tens to hundreds of megawatts and sells its tenants a four-nines availability SLA — roughly 52 minutes of permitted downtime a year. A sustained curtailment is a direct breach, and power is already the single largest cause of significant data-centre outages.{{cite:ACAD-DC-OUTAGE,INDUSTRY-DC-COMPUTE-DEMAND}}

Scale the stack from three directions that rarely meet in one briefing. Demand: Ofgem's demand CFI and NESO queue data put tens of gigawatts of new load in front of a constrained network, disproportionately on flexible terms.{{cite:OFGEM-DEMAND-REFORM,ACAD-DESANTI-FCA-QUEUE}} Constraint cost: NESO's published constraint-cost series shows the system operator already paying for curtailment — a lower bound on frequency economics the BI tower does not see.{{cite:NESO-CONSTRAINT-COSTS}} Premium runway: carrier and broker research sizes hyperscale insurable values toward double-digit billions in premium pool by decade-end — but almost entirely on damage-first forms.{{cite:SP-HYPERSCALE-INSURABLE-POOL,SWISS-RE-DATA-CENTRE-AI,BROK-MARSH-NIMBUS}} Sources disagree on timing; they agree the insured base is moving faster than the trigger layer.

The financial value at risk is contracted load times hours off times the penalty rate per hour — the same identity actuaries use to price long-outage SLA cover.{{cite:ACAD-EXPONENTIAL-PARETO-SLA-PREMIUM,INDUSTRY-PARAMETRIC-DC-FINANCING}} None of those terms appears in a physical-damage policy. Curtailment cost is already observable in the system operator's constraint-cost data;{{cite:NESO-CONSTRAINT-COSTS}} the market carries an exposure whose severity it does not compute and whose frequency it does not track. The premium that should attach to availability cover is a function the existing book never evaluates; the premium that does attach is zero, because the cover does not exist.
The market is not underpricing this peril. It is not pricing it at all.
VII · Wedge, not vendor
Wedge, not vendor

The cat-model instinct is to reduce a risk to a single number and rank the market by it. For this peril that instinct misranks the field — and misstates concentration, because two exposed names on the same constrained network are not independent exposures.{{cite:ACT-HHI-EIOPA,INDUSTRY-AGGREGATION-CONUNDRUM}} The same non-firm exposure is well-carried by an underwriter with the data, products, modelling and capital to hold it, and dangerous in the hands of one without. A one-axis score cannot express that, because it collapses the two things whose difference is the entire signal.

The map is a wedge, not the product: the proprietary, primary-source understanding of a peril the rest of the market underwrites blind. The measured features — connection-gate status, flexible-connection share, aggregation over shared grid geography, trigger gap against parametric availability — are built to be exactly the edge that lets you price the gap and carry it.{{cite:BROK-LOCKTON-SLA,DESCARTES-DC-PARAMETRIC,MGA-PARAMETRIX-SLA}} Whoever holds that picture first is positioned not to sell a score, but to write the cover that does not yet exist.
VIII · Rules land first
When firmness becomes a fact

Connections reform is converting firmness into a dated, registered fact. As the queue moves to a gated model, an asset's firmness becomes an objective register entry: which gate it sits behind, on what terms, with what curtailment rights attached.{{cite:NESO-CMP434,NESO-CMP448,NESO-GC0166}} Live rules already in force — CMP434/448 for Gate 1 and Gate 2 progression, GC0166 for limited-duration dispatch — start re-pricing the same sub-factors on every renewal, without waiting for a consultation to close.

Demand-side reform adds the second leg. Ofgem's consultation on very-large-user curtailment rights would make interruptibility a negotiable commercial fact for the largest campuses — not only a connection-offer footnote.{{cite:OFGEM-DEMAND-REFORM}} Gate-2 queue fees already price progression into firmer access; when an asset steps from Gate 1 to Gate 2, non-firm intensity and aggregation sub-factors move in the scoring pipeline without waiting for a renewal meeting. The market that still rates on damage history will look mispriced the quarter register facts update.
IX · Measure to carry
Measure it, then carry it

Parametric availability, SLA mirrors, curtailment indices — the fragments exist. No one yet holds the full stack: measured non-firm exposure, basis-minimised trigger, aggregation-aware pricing, and rated paper in whitespace.

No other public dataset plots {{fact:total}} UK market participants on the same exposure and preparedness construct with register-native sub-factors and downloadable provenance — cat vendors map hazards, brokers map facilities, parametric MGAs map products. The index is the field map for a peril that cuts across all three: who is exposed beyond their means, who has capacity in whitespace, and which linked assets diverge from the carrier headline. That map is the prerequisite for the cover — not the cover itself.

The market deploys capacity onto whoever looks exposed on a damage view, while genuine non-firm losses concentrate where exposure has outrun preparedness — and rated capital with specialist product still sits in whitespace because the trigger layer has not caught up to the grid.{{cite:SP-HYPERSCALE-INSURABLE-POOL,SP-INSURANCE-GAP-HYPERSCALE}} The scatter is that divergence made visible: each dot is a posture on two axes, and whitespace is where cover can still be written before queue repricing closes the window.
